chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Horace Henderson's band; the 1933 Berlin summer contract
summary: Returning in 1929 after Fowler and Roberts, Butler joined Horace Henderson's band, playing his brother's music at college proms and parties at the Dunbar Palace until about 1933-34. He then took a summer contract at the Feminina in Berlin in 1933.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Oh, there's one thing I wanted to clear up, you told me at the bar one time. You told me about a time when -- well, we'll talk about "Paris Blues" later. This is a story you told me about Ellington.
Well, now, I've left -- I went with Billy Fowler's band.
You mean you went back with Billy Fowler's band?
No, I went with Billy Fowler's band, I had come back in '29. Now Horace Henderson, Fletcher Henderson's brother, he assembled a band. And so I got in that band.
So this was after Lucky Roberts?

Yeah, after Lucky Roberts and after Billy Fowler. I got in Horace Henderson's band. And we were working a place called Dunbar Palace, it was a place where people get -- well, it was a dance in the evening, you could all the sorority clubs give them parties and balls there. dance, you know. And you give--for, And the band is a beautiful band. In fact, we had the same music that his brother had. Horace would steal his brother's music but Horace was a beautiful arranger. And he had all this beautiful music. And the music that we played was something like the music I played in Washington, D. C. Because when we played for these parties, college proms and things, you played that kind of music.

So we played, stayed together for quite some time. Until about 1933 or something like that, '34. Now in the meantime, I'd met a man and he asked me (inaudible). So I said, yes, if you play me a certain salary. And I was there. The big solo was to play "Dinah," and "St. Louis Blues" and things like that.
Well, there was a place in Berlin called the Feminina.
Okay, let me turn this tape over.
1933 or something. About the end of '33. This was a very short stay, the contract was for the summer season.
